title: Adentris vs Lyssn: Session Quality vs Revenue Integrity Compared
summary: Adentris vs Lyssn for behavioral health and SUD: AI session-quality and fidelity scoring versus real-time revenue integrity and documentation compliance with ASAM, 42 CFR Part 2, and appeals.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Lyssn and Adentris both use AI in behavioral health, but they solve different problems. Lyssn analyzes recorded sessions to score how closely a clinician follows evidence-based practices like CBT and motivational interviewing, for quality assurance and training. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note in real time before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module built in. If your problem is care quality and clinician training, Lyssn is built for that. If your problem is denials and audit exposure, that is where Adentris focuses.


They aim at different jobs, one at care quality and one at getting paid, so the comparison is about which problem is costing you now. Here is the honest breakdown.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What Lyssn does


Lyssn is an AI platform for behavioral health that analyzes recorded sessions and scores clinician fidelity to evidence-based practices such as cognitive behavioral therapy and motivational interviewing, using validated rating scales. It gives supervisors and quality teams a fast, objective way to measure care quality and support training, in minutes rather than the hours a human rater would take. For organizations focused on clinical quality, fidelity, and workforce development, Lyssn is a strong, research-backed option.

Capabilities change quickly in this market, so confirm current details with each vendor before you decide.


## Which should you choose?


Lyssn is built around clinical quality: measuring how faithfully sessions follow evidence-based practices so supervisors can coach and improve care. Adentris is built around revenue integrity: making sure the documentation supports the claim so behavioral health and SUD programs get paid. It flags a missing medical necessity statement, an unjustified ASAM level of care, or a missing 42 CFR Part 2 consent, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs review with an appeals and denials module. The two do not overlap much: one improves the therapy, the other protects the revenue, and a program can run both.


- **Choose Lyssn if** you want an objective, research-backed way to measure session quality and clinician fidelity to evidence-based practices for QA and training.
- **Choose Adentris if** your problem is denied claims and audit exposure, and you want documentation checked against payer and regulatory denial criteria before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 depth and an appeals workflow, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a Lyssn alternative for revenue integrity


Lyssn and Adentris are not really alternatives; they solve different problems. If what you actually need is fewer denied claims and less audit exposure rather than session-quality scoring, that is where Adentris fits: it reviews the documentation against payer and regulatory denial criteria, drafts the correction before submission, and pairs that with an appeals and denials workflow, running on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent. Many programs run a quality tool like Lyssn and a revenue-integrity layer like Adentris side by side.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. ## The bottom line


Lyssn measures the quality of the therapy; Adentris protects the revenue behind it. They solve different problems and can run together: use Lyssn for fidelity and training, and Adentris to make sure behavioral health and SUD claims get paid.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and Lyssn?**


Lyssn analyzes recorded behavioral health sessions to score clinician fidelity to evidence-based practices like CBT and motivational interviewing, for quality assurance and training. Adentris is a revenue integrity and documentation compliance layer that reviews the note before the claim is submitted, with SUD-specific rules like ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals module. Lyssn measures care quality; Adentris makes sure the claim gets paid.


**Can Adentris and Lyssn be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use Lyssn to measure session quality and fidelity and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside Lyssn.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to Lyssn?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than care quality and clinician training, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. Lyssn is strong for measuring session fidelity to evidence-based practices. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
